sense: a couple of: two or so, a few

terms.grammar: phrase: both words agree with the noun
evidence: Cic. Clu. 72: ūnus et alter diēs intercesserat
Hor. Ep. 2.1.74: versus paulō concinnior ūnus et alter (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: of an indefinite number, one and another, one or two. Also ūnus alterve: ūnum alterumve diem, a day or two (Cic. Fam. 3.9.2).

phrases.english: a day or two had gone by

phrases.latin: cēnābis bene, mī Fabulle, apud mē paucīs, sī tibi dī favent, diēbus
phrases.english: you’ll dine well at my house, Fabullus, in a couple of days, if the gods are kind to you

sources: Lewis & Short: unus · Lewis & Short: alter · Lewis & Short: paucus
